name: Human albumin
executiveSummary: Colloid. Adult: **0.5–1 g/kg**. Pediatric shock: 5% albumin **5–10 mL/kg** (**0.25–0.5 g/kg**). Neonates: **0.5–1 g/kg** (or 5% **10–20 mL/kg**) slow IV.
indications:
## Indications

- Selected volume expansion; burns; large-volume paracentesis.

## Precautions

- Fluid overload; rare allergy.

> Does not replace crystalloids as first line in most shocks.

adulto.dose: 0.5–1 g/kg per indication (paracentesis: 6–8 g/L of ascites removed).

pediatrico.dose: Shock: 5% albumin in NS = 5–10 mL/kg (0.25–0.50 g/kg). Max dose: 6 g/kg/day
pediatrico.presentation: See albumin evidence-based use (CIME bulletin). 50 mL vial at 20%
pediatrico.notes: Infusion rate: 0.25–1 mL/min. See Colloid Solutions (CIME bulletin).

neonatal.dose: Hypoalbuminemia / selected expansion: **0.5–1 g/kg** IV (orient. equiv. 5% albumin **10–20 mL/kg** or 20% **2.5–5 mL/kg**) slow over 1–2 h.
neonatal.administration: Slow IV; do not mix with other drugs in the same line.

stability:
## Stability

- Use immediately after spiking; do not mix with other drugs.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Heart failure from volume overload, urticaria.
